title: Interleaved-slice batcher: scheduler tuning for mixed prompt/response dialogs, KV reservation, and GPU fragmentation
creator: Jamal Ortiz
description: Goal: Implement and validate an interleaved-slice batcher for mixed prompt/response workloads that improves P50/P95 latency for short-turn dialogs while preserving throughput for long responses. Scope covers scheduler policy changes, KV cache reservation heuristics to avoid prefix eviction, and GPU slab tuning to reduce fragmentation under heterogeneous sequence length loads. Deliverables: design doc, canary runtime build, perf dashboard, rollout plan and rollback criteria.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Jamal Ortiz: Created ticket after a spike showed repeated P99 regressions when short prompts were coalesced with very long responses. Hypothesis: current continuous scheduler prioritizes batch fullness over interleaving which causes head-of-line blocking and KV churn.

2026-02-12 - Sofia Nguyen: Ran workload trace analysis on production sampled traces (last 24h). Observed dialog length bimodality: 62% short (<64 tokens), 28% mid (64-512), 10% long (>1024). KV cache churn increases by ~18% on mixed batches causing ~7% additional GPU memcpy and higher fragmentation.

2026-02-18 - Eng spike: Built two prototypes: (A) strict-priority slice splitter that isolates short prompts into dedicated micro-slots; (B) interleaved-slice batcher that allows small slices to preempt coalescing of large sequences with a weight-decay fairness. Microbenchmarks: (A) reduces P95 for shorts by 26% but hurts throughput on long-only workloads by 9%. (B) achieves balanced 12% P95 improvement for shorts and <2% throughput loss on long-only.

2026-02-22 - Design decision: Proceed with prototype (B) interleaved-slice batcher as primary approach. Rationale: better trade-off for customer workloads that mix short assistant queries and long generation tasks. Will add tunable preemption window and weight decay constants as runtime flags.
2026-02-24 - PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Interleaved+Slice+Batcher+Design (design doc with sequencing diagrams and metric targets).

2026-02-26 - Engineering note: KV reservation heuristic: reserve a fraction of KV slab for active short-turn slots (configurable per-model). Implemented LRU-with-reservation to avoid prefix thrash from long-response tokens. Edge case: some long responses still evict reserved space under memory pressure -> introduced soft-reservation with eviction penalty scoring.

2026-03-01 - GPU tuning: Adjusted slab allocator bucket sizes and introduced coalescing-friendly free lists to reduce fragmentation from repeated allocate/free patterns of large KV segments. Observed 4-6% GPU memory headroom recovery on load tests.

2026-03-02 - Canary results: Canary on dedicated pool (region-us-west-2, model: open-redwood-phi-7B-quant) over 12h: short-turn P95 reduced 11%, P99 reduced 6%. End-to-end throughput for mixed workload stable (-1.5%). Memory reserve violated on 2 out of 50 stress tests; protection path correctly throttled long-response slots and logged alerts.

2026-03-03 - Review feedback (PM/Infra): PM requests clearer rollout gating for customer-impacted SLAs; Infra asks to add more exportable metrics around KV-reservation-hit-rate and fragmentation ratio. Action: add two dashboards and a kill-switch config in the operator.

2026-03-03 - Next steps: finalize runtime flags, add dashboards (grafana link placeholders), prepare canary rollout plan, write runbook for anomalies, and open follow-up ticket for tightening eviction policy after extended soak.
acceptance_criteria: Short-turn P95 improves >=10% on mixed-dialog workload without increasing long-response P95 by >5%
KV reservation hit-rate > 85% under mixed load in canary
No unexplained increase in GPU OOMs or sustained memory pressure during 48h soak
Runtime flag allows instant rollback to prior scheduler behavior
